stem:
Rina compares two triangles that share two pairs of equal corresponding sides and one pair of equal corresponding angles that is not between those sides.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Conclude the triangles must be congruent from those matches alone, skipping that the equal angle is not the included angle.
Treat that side-side-angle match as a congruence test for every polygon, not only as a failed triangle test.
Those matches do not always guarantee congruence; the same data can fit two non-congruent triangles.
Claim congruence only because the word equal is repeated often in the stem.

teacher.key_rationale: Two sides and a non-included equal angle do not force a unique triangle, so congruence is not guaranteed. Treating the matches as enough, stretching the failed test to every polygon, or grabbing a repeated surface word all miss that limit.
